classification.difficultyReason: Calculate two triangle areas and explain their equality using supplementary-angle sine values.

content.prompt: Find the area of these two triangles, correct to 2 decimal places.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle with a vertical left side, right-hand vertex and an included angle at the lower-left vertex.
spec.mathematics: The sides enclosing the 60° angle are 20 cm and 15 cm. Coordinates use a common proportional unit of 10 cm.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied lengths and angle are visible; no area answer is included.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle with a vertical left side and a lower-right vertex. The obtuse included angle retains its arc and leader arrow.
spec.mathematics: The sides enclosing the 120° angle are 20 cm and 15 cm. Coordinates use the same proportional unit as Triangle 1.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied lengths and angle are visible; no area answer is included.

children.prompt: What do you notice? How can you explain this?

answer.worked: Both triangles have the same two enclosing side lengths. Their included angles are supplementary, so $\sin120^{\circ}=\sin(180^{\circ}-60^{\circ})=\sin60^{\circ}$. Hence $\tfrac12(20)(15)\sin C$ gives the same area for both triangles.
